These three domains share family a.298.1.1 because SCOPe classifies them by the shared architecture of the TAL effector repeat module, not by total chain length. Each TAL effector repeat is a tandem module of about 33-35 residues forming a helix-loop-helix unit. Tandem repeats of this unit pack into a continuous right-handed superhelical solenoid. Naturally occurring Xanthomonas TAL effectors and their engineered derivatives carry a variable number of repeats, often from about 1.5 to over 30, and may include or omit flanking N- and C-terminal regions. The length differences among d2kq5a_ (PDB 2KQ5, chain A), d3v6pa_ (PDB 3V6P, chain A), and d4cj9a_ (PDB 4CJ9, chain A) therefore most likely reflect repeat copy number and construct boundaries. They do not indicate a different fold or family. Each domain is a copy-number variant of the same helical repeat solenoid, and the family-level signal is the repeated helix-turn-helix packing that all three share.

Level of evolutionary strength: a.298.1.1 is a family (fourth level). It sits inside superfamily a.298.1 and fold a.298 (class a, all-alpha). Shared family membership supports a common repeat-based architecture and homology at the family level. It does not establish that the three structures have the same DNA-target specificity, the same residue-to-base recognition code, or the same biological function. Those properties depend on the repeat-variable diresidues (RVDs, typically at repeat positions 12 and 13), which are not used to assign SCOPe family.

Limits and unsafe transfers: do not transfer DNA-binding specificity, target-site prediction, or engineering design rules from family membership alone. Those require the actual RVD sequence and experimental or structural evidence for the specific construct. Whether a given structure is DNA-bound, its repeat count, and its exact domain boundaries are release-specific facts. Confirming them requires the SCOPe release domain file and the PDB entries, which I did not access here. I also did not verify the exact fold or superfamily name text from SCOPe. Structure-based family membership is also not a proxy for sequence identity: repeats within an array are similar at the scaffold level but diverge in sequence, so sequence-length differences should not be read as evidence against shared family.
